chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who has a debt upon another man, so he says to him before the term becomes due: 'Expedite for me half of my right, on condition that I remit the other half from you.' Is that permissible for one of them? He said: 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to forgive part of a debt in exchange for early payment of the rest?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the validity of 'salam' or early settlement agreements where a creditor accepts partial immediate payment in exchange for forgiving the remainder, a practice known as *ta'wil*. It reflects the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence for resolving debts amicably before maturity, emphasizing mutual consent over rigid contractual terms. This ruling is often cited in discussions of *fiqh al-mu'amalat* to demonstrate how financial obligations can be modified by agreement prior to the due date.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban, from the one who narrated it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who happened to have a debt for him upon the man, so he is saying to him before the expiry of the term, ‘Give half to me from my right and I shall drop from you the (other) half’. Is that Permissible for one of them (to do)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Aban from those who narrated to him who has said the following:

“I once asked the Imam, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man to whom another man owed a certain amount of loan who before the due date asked the borrower to pay him half of the loan so he then might cancel the other half in favor of the borrower. He (the Imam) said, ‘Such settlement is lawful.”
